subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw-hooks helper processes orphaned when a run terminates abnormally

question: Should this remain an OpenClaw repair after a current-version process-tree reproduction, or should the exact orphaning behavior be routed to the Codex runtime owner if OpenClaw only configures the relay command?
rationale: The current integration configures and registers relay commands, but the dependency runtime launches the hook subprocesses; choosing a process-group or parent-death mechanism without proving ownership could broaden shutdown behavior incorrectly.

options.title: Obtain current process-tree proof
options.body: Reproduce against v2026.7.1 or current main and capture PID, PPID, PGID, command line, and survival duration for the gateway, Codex app-server, and relay helpers.

options.title: Route to Codex ownership
options.body: If the capture shows the surviving helpers are owned by the Codex runtime after OpenClaw exits, file or link the dependency-runtime bug instead of adding a core process reaper.

recommendation.title: Obtain current process-tree proof
recommendation.body: Reproduce against v2026.7.1 or current main and capture PID, PPID, PGID, command line, and survival duration for the gateway, Codex app-server, and relay helpers.

likelyOwner.reason: Their current-main lifecycle work is the closest proven ownership signal for timeout, relay, and helper command behavior.
